fun_highlights: The card pool is genuinely large (138 cards) with meaningful gating: 14 callback cards, 6 era cards, 3 vocation-x-era intersections, 4 fate events, 8 trait-moment cards, 4 seat-gated cards, 5 repute-gated cards, 7 competing-goods dilemmas — large swaths of content a given life will never see.

Vocation gating (soldier/scholar/maker/wanderer) creates structurally distinct adult arcs: a soldier's war ghost at 3am, a scholar's unanswered question, a maker's masterwork, a wanderer's reckoning — these read as different shapes of life, not the same template with new labels.

Era system (war/plague/hard/plenty/turning/settled) works as genuine context drift. A soldier in a war era gets vx_soldier_war, which is rarer and weightier than standard soldier content. Dynasty 4 (Renner) running across a war era felt substantively different from Dynasty 2 (Sereno) in plenty.

Discovery count on the title screen (N of 138 moments witnessed) is exactly the right signal for a completionist: it names the scale of the unseen pool without spoiling what is in it. This is a genuine reason to keep playing.

Callback cards are the game's best mechanic: the child who kept the stray and gets it back as an epitaph cluster; the child_books heirloom returning three generations later; the unspoken love resurfacing in midlife. These feel earned, not random — a completionist will want to see all 14.

Housechar and houseAspirations give a concrete forward-facing list ('still ahead: words the family can live by; a line six generations deep') — the completionist pull is explicit and well-constructed.

onceDyn burning cards dynasty-wide means each new house still has a first encounter with the founding-hardship and defining-dilemma beats. The pool resets per house, keeping early dynasties feeling fresh.
Solitary/childless life-shapes (m_solitary, e_solitary, e_childless) are real content, not empty outcomes — a completionist wanting to see every branch needs to intentionally close love paths.
The meta-progression layer (houses raised list, motto collection, discovery count) across runs provides a tangible record of what the completionist has built, which is satisfying to accumulate.
staleness: Across 18 dynasties, five cards surface in nearly every single life regardless of vocation or trait: y_calling (vocation fork), a_child (child question), a_marry (marriage), m_parent_age (aging parent), e_legacy (what to be remembered for). These are high-weight anchor cards that the draw engine nudges strongly toward. A completionist will have seen all five within two or three dynasties and will see them in virtually every life thereafter — they are structural wallpaper by dynasty 6.

The cb_reckless and cb_the_cost elder callbacks appear in a large fraction of transcripts because their conditions (lived_reckless, chose_self/chose_others/chose_loyalty) are triggered by several common paths. They feel less like rare discoveries and more like near-guaranteed elder content.

Scholar lives are over-represented across the 18 dynasties in the transcripts — seven of the eighteen dynasties have at least one scholar — because y_calling has equal weight on all four vocations but the scholar_study callback chain (cb_study_pays, a_scholar_question, m_scholar_legacy, e_scholar_old) adds four extra cards making that path notably longer and more visible than the wanderer path, which has fewer exclusive mid-life beats.

The discovery count on the title screen shows 'N of 138' but a player has no granular signal of which categories remain unseen. A completionist wants to know 'I have seen 2 of 6 era cards' or 'I have seen 5 of 14 callbacks' — the aggregate total is less actionable than a category breakdown would be. Without this, the sense of chase is present but imprecise.

Seat-7 ('a house written into the histories') is the completionist's summit but the conditions (seat-6 house, repPeak >= 3.5, peakMeans >= 76, 45% chance) mean it requires a very focused multi-dynasty run and may not trigger even when conditions are met. In 18 dynasties across the transcripts, no house reached seat-7 — the summit is visible but no playthrough landed there, making it feel possible-in-theory rather than achievable-in-practice.

Repute mottos can repeat across dynasties — Dynasty 4 (Renner) and Dynasty 12 (Ashby) both crystallize 'We earn the bread we eat'; Dynasty 2 (Sereno) and Dynasty 13 (Reyes) both get 'Better a short blaze and a long smoke'. The MOTTOS table has 3 variants per reputation type but those are not being drawn freshly enough across dynasties to prevent repetition in a single extended session.

The 'competing goods' dilemma cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty, x_promise, x_mercy, x_favour) are excellent in isolation but their cond gates are broad — x_honest_or_kind fires on any rel with bond > 45, which most lives have by midlife. In practice these run once per life on cooldown rather than feeling rare.

No visible inventory of unlocked heirlooms, earned mottos, or seen epitaph clusters exists across all runs (only the titles-screen motto list and discovery count). A completionist wants to know which of the 9 reputation-type mottos they have crystallised, which of the 5 heirloom types they have passed down, and which epitaph clusters they have seen — the absence makes cross-run progress opaque.

improvements.what: Add a category-level discovery breakdown on the title screen or constellation: show 'Callbacks seen: 5/14 | Era moments: 3/6 | Vocation x Era: 1/3 | Fate: 2/4 | Trait: 4/8' instead of (or alongside) the single aggregate count.
improvements.why: A completionist knows there is more to find but cannot aim at specific gaps. Category counts give a concrete hunt: 'I have never played a plague era, never seen the seat-gated s_patronage card.' This turns the discovery system from a vague progress bar into a real collection challenge without spoiling card text.

improvements.what: Reduce the weight of the five template anchors (y_calling, a_child, a_marry, m_parent_age, e_legacy) or cap how strongly the engine nudges them, so a larger fraction of a life is drawn from the mid-tier and rarer pool.
improvements.why: These five fire in 80-90% of lives, making them structural wallpaper rather than moments. Lowering their engine nudge from near-certain to probable (say, 60-70%) would let the rarer cards surface more often per life, reducing the sense that every life hits the same five beats before getting to the interesting variation.

improvements.what: Add one or two more midlife cards exclusive to the wanderer and maker vocations to bring their late-career depth up to the scholar's arc (currently scholar has 4 exclusive mid-life cards: a_scholar_question, m_scholar_legacy, e_scholar_old, vx_scholar_turning; wanderer has 2: a_wanderer_settle, m_wanderer_return).
improvements.why: Vocation choice is supposed to be the major structural differentiator but wanderer and maker have thinner mid-life content than scholar, making those paths feel shorter and less characterful. A completionist who discovers this will feel the asymmetry and be less motivated to pursue those arcs.

improvements.what: Add a cross-run 'Dynasties Compendium' view (accessible from the title screen) that shows the full list of earned mottos, heirloom types collected, epitaph clusters witnessed, and seat-peak reached, persisted across all houses via localStorage.
improvements.why: The completionist's primary joy is knowing what they have found and seeing what remains. The current meta-persistence (houses list, discovery count) is minimal. A compendium that showed 'Mottos unlocked: 4/9 — scholarly, kind, industrious, generous' would make the long-game collection loop explicit and satisfying without spoiling content.

improvements.what: Make seat-7 ('a house written into the histories') slightly more achievable or signal its path more clearly in houseAspirations — currently the conditions are underdocumented and no house in 18 dynasties reached it.
improvements.why: The summit a completionist most wants to reach appears unreachable in practice during a normal extended session. Either lower the 45% chance gate, make repPeak cumulative across dynasties (not resetting), or surface a clearer readable trajectory ('the name is at 3.1 — the histories need 3.5 and the seat raised to 6') so the climb feels tractable.

verdict: A Life is a genuinely large, well-gated content library with a real completionist pull — 138 cards, 14 callbacks, 6 eras, layered dynasty arcs — but five near-universal template cards appear in almost every life, the discovery signal lacks category granularity, and seat-7 remains unreachable in practice, leaving a completionist who has played 6+ dynasties feeling they have seen the skeleton of every life even as the rare content stays genuinely elusive.
